text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Croat member of Bosnian collective presidency Kresimir Zubak asks U.N. war crimes tribunal to dismiss Vasvija Vidovic, Bosnian government liason official to the tribunal, because he says she was not appointed by Federation authorities. Moslem chairman of the presidency, Alija Izetbegovic says Vidovic is legally named to her post.

- Representatives of the international community in Bosnia welcome the reported arrest of those believed to be linked with mafia in the Croat part of divided Bosnian town of Mostar but say that the arrests must be confirmed.
- The interior minister of the Herzegovina-Neretva County, Valentin Coric, reduces curfew imposed in Mostar after recent violence. The curfew will begin from 11 p.m. instead of 9 p.m.

- Bosnia's ruling Moslem Party of Democratic Action (SDA) welcomes the international police report on the Mostar incident and says that this report could represent a step forward in reviving the Moslem-Croat Federation.

- Information bureau for planned visit of Pope John Paul II was closed shortly after it opened due to anonymous telephone threats that Pope will be killed if he dares to visit Sarajevo, the Catholic Press Agency (KTA) says in a statement. The church planned to reopen office on Friday.

- The Bosnian Council of Ministers adopts a draft law on foreign debts and debates a law on custom taxes. It agrees that the entities of Bosnia will take responsibility for the debt which will be overseen by the foreign trade ministry.
- Office of the Moslem-Croat Federation ombudsmen confirms that Saint Theresa's Church in Moslem-controlled town of Donji Vakuf was dynamited overnight, causing minor structural demage.
- Sarajevo county officials accept a $780,000 loan from the Malaysian government for housing reconstruction. -- Sarajevo newsroom +387-71-663-864
